newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says to maintain relations with Burma.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says to maintain relations with Burma.

text.p: Malaysia will maintain its relations with the Burmese military government and continue a dialogue with it despite recent events, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Saturday.

He was quoted by news agency Bernama as saying there was evidence of change in the Rangoon military junta which was opening up the country under the efforts of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).

"Myanmar (Burma) is a rich country. If we shut them off, they can live for years without any contact with the rest of the world," he was quoted as telling reporters after opening the Gerakan party's national convention.

"In fact, that was what they did for almost 20 years, why was there no effort to block them then?" he said in reaction to the United States ban on Burma's military rulers and their families travelling to the U.S.
The U.S. action follows Burma's latest crackdown on the democracy movement in which hundreds of supporters of opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi have been detained.
Mahathir said unlike the U.S., Malaysia preferred to interact and have meaningful dialogue with Burma.
He said if Burma joined ASEAN, other members of the grouping would be able to have some influence on the Rangoon regime.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand. Burma, Laos and Cambodia are expected to join this grouping in the next few years.
Gerakan is a mainly ethnic Chinese party that forms part of Mahathir's multi-racial National Front.
